# Feature 1: comment editing

Endpoint: PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id with body {"comment":{"body":"..."}}. Changes the body text. Who may edit, when, and what the edit marks come from the rules below.

Rules (name: source; values deliberately omitted):
- auth-header: code-auth-header. Caller identity from the Authorization header.
- comment-ownership: code-comment-ownership. Owner is the authorId field.
- comment-model: code-comment-model. Current Comment fields.
- edit-window: policy-edit-window. Time limit on editing after creation.
- edited-marker: policy-edited-at-marker. editedAt field; its migration must not change existing rows.
- error-body: policy-error-response. Body shape for new error responses.
- error-codes-today: code-error-shape. Status codes already in use. Its body shapes are not used for new errors.
- migrations: code-migrations. Folder, naming, apply command, database address variable.
- release-checklist: policy-release-checklist. Fresh-database check and undo note per migration.
- test-layout: code-test-layout. Unit test location, run command, database mock.

Conflict: code-comment-ownership returns an empty body for a not-allowed delete. policy-error-response requires the errors-object body for new errors. Followed policy-error-response for the body. Status code still open.

Open items (no rule found; none invented):
- Status code for an edit refused by edit-window.
- Status code when the comment is missing or owned by someone else on edit.

content.text:
The comment edit change now follows the edit-window rule. I could not run the tests or the migration in this session, so they are checked by reading only.

**Question 1:** A comment author may edit their own comment for 30 minutes after it was created (`policy-edit-window`). After that the API refuses the edit.

**Change made:** The working tree used 15 minutes. I changed it to 30 minutes in `app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts` (`COMMENT_EDIT_WINDOW_MS`). In `app/src/tests/services/comment-edit.service.test.ts` I updated the test names and times: the "inside the window" case now uses 29 minutes, and the "refused" case uses 31 minutes.

**Rules checked and whether the code follows them:**

| Rule | Value | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edit window | 30 minutes after creation | `policy-edit-window` | Fixed (was 15) |
| Edited marker | Nullable `editedAt`, null until first edit, set on each successful edit. Migration must not change existing rows. | `policy-edited-at-marker` | Follows. The column is nullable and the migration only runs `ADD COLUMN`. |
| Migration undo note | One-line undo note per migration | `policy-release-checklist` | Follows. The migration file has `-- Undo: ALTER TABLE "Comment" DROP COLUMN "editedAt";`. |
| Migration folder and naming | One timestamped folder under `app/src/prisma/migrations` | `code-migrations` | Follows. The folder is `20261030120000_comment_edited_at`. |
| Comment owner | `authorId` | `code-comment-ownership` | Follows. The lookup filters by `authorId`. |
| Test location and mock | `*.test.ts` under `app/src/tests/services`, database mocked by `prisma-mock.ts` | `code-test-layout` | Follows. |
| Error body for new errors | `{"errors":{"<field>":["message"]}}` with no wrapper | `policy-error-response` | The 422 and 404 bodies follow it. |

**Open items I did not change:**
- **Status code for an edit refused by the window.** No rule sets it, and the spec lists it as open. The code still throws a plain `Error`, so the handler returns 500 with the message as a plain string body. That does not match the errors-object body rule. Fixing it needs a status code from the team.
- **Status code for a missing or not-owned comment on edit.** The code returns 404 with the errors-object body. The 404 is taken from the delete rule, not from an edit rule, and the spec lists this status as open. The test asserts 404, so it will need to change if the team picks another code.

**Rule sources:** all values come from the team notes named above, as given in the task. The spec is `specs/feature-1-comment-editing.md`. The spec also records a conflict between `code-comment-ownership` (empty 404 body) and `policy-error-response` (errors-object body). The spec resolved it in favor of `policy-error-response`, and the code follows that.
